1	# STDO Representation Product
     2	
     3	Status: active source definition repricing release-matched `2.5.0` to exact
     4	Source STDO `v2.5.0-rc.2`; accepted STDO Representation
     5	`stdo_representation/v2.5.0-rc.1` remains immutable.
     6	
     7	## Product statement
     8	
     9	STDO Representation 2.5.0 is the canonical `a_c.STDO` semantic compression of
    10	exact Source STDO 2.5.0, the deterministic logical constraint index over that
    11	compression, and concise native instructions for using both. An LLM reads
    12	Source STDO, authors the compression, invokes the released Axiom Indexer
    13	validator, repairs diagnostics, and uses the index to select reference frames
    14	and prepare bounded work.
    15	
    16	The Product adds no local semantic compiler, GTL engine, prompt orchestrator,
    17	or model runtime. Exact Axiom Indexer supplies all deterministic mechanics. The
    18	LLM remains the semantic harness and supplies every frame, label, text value,
    19	and ordering choice.
    20	
    21	## Product shape
    22	
    23	```text
    24	exact Source STDO 2.5.0
    25	  -> a_c.STDO 2.5.0 Axiomatic Program (semantic compression)
    26	  -> Logical Constraint Map (deterministic index over the program)
    27	  -> native STDO Representation skill
    28	  -> LLM-selected visible frame details and ordered sections
    29	  -> Axiom Indexer pure join
    30	  -> bounded Codex or Claude work with source re-entry
    31	```
    32	
    33	The program and map are derived from Source STDO. They do not replace or amend
    34	it.
    35	
    36	## Product terms
    37	
    38	- **Represented STDO Version** is semantic version line `2.5.0`; its exact
    39	  represented cut is immutable STDO `v2.5.0-rc.2`.
    40	- **Source STDO** is that exact installed standards corpus and remains semantic
    41	  authority.
    42	- **Axiom Indexer Dependency** is exact accepted Axiom Indexer
    43	  `v0.1.0-rc.1`, used without copying its Product members into this Product.
    44	- **Shared-Source Release Profile** is this Product's stable Project Release
    45	  Namespace and project-qualified ref selection under the installed Release
    46	  Method. It owns Git transport spelling and Project Subtree coordinates, not
    47	  Product meaning or membership.
    48	- **`a_c.STDO` Axiomatic Program** is the canonical semantic compression
    49	  selected for the exact represented cut. It contains URI-identified symbols,
    50	  clauses, and residuals grounded in Source STDO.
    51	- **Logical Constraint Map** is the deterministic Axiom Indexer index

   165	## Authoring and validation relation

    11	## Purpose
    12	
    13	Let an LLM author `a_c.STDO`, invoke exact Axiom Indexer validation, consume all
    14	mechanical diagnostics, and write a new candidate when repair is needed.
    15	
    16	## Relation
    17	
    18	```text
    19	LLMAuthor(Source_STDO, authoring_contract, selected_frames)
    20	  -> Program* | hold | residual
    21	
    22	AxiomValidate(Compression*, BindingSet)
    23	  -> valid compression + bound LogicalConstraintIndex | diagnostics
    24	```
    25	
    26	The LLM performs semantic interpretation and repair. Axiom Indexer performs the
    27	released deterministic relation over unchanged bytes. No local STDO
    28	Representation compiler or validator is added.
    29	
    30	## Imported validation boundary
    31	
    32	The exact dependency checks:
    33	
    34	- the closed Axiomatic Program shape;
    35	- absolute and unique URIs;
    36	- sorted, duplicate-free URI sets and program item populations;
    37	- local reference closure and declared vocabulary/frame domains;
    38	- source and frame URI resolution through the Binding Set;
    39	- non-empty source grounding;
    40	- residual subject and re-entry closure; and
    41	- deterministic program and logical-map identity.
    42	
    43	It does not check prose truth, completeness, unique interpretation, automatic
    44	frame applicability, or a complete admitted `a_c` algebra.
    45	
    46	## Requirements
    47	
    48	**REQ-P-CANDIDATE-001**: Authoring shall use exact Source STDO, the exact Axiom
    49	Indexer output contract and schema, selected authoring frames, and explicit
    50	source bindings. Missing material input shall produce a hold or residual rather
    51	than invented meaning.
    52	
    53	**REQ-P-CANDIDATE-002**: The LLM shall capture essential symbols, relations,
    54	constraints, and uncertainty. It shall not satisfy the Product by mechanically
    55	restating every source paragraph or by claiming unsupported completeness.
    56	
    57	**REQ-P-CANDIDATE-003**: Validation shall invoke the exact released Axiom
    58	Indexer executable and preserve the candidate bytes. No STDO Representation
    59	script shall fork, widen, or silently patch the imported contract.
    60	
    61	**REQ-P-CANDIDATE-004**: Every safely detectable diagnostic shall be returned
    62	to the LLM. A crash, unresolved dependency, invalid binding, parse failure, or
    63	partial evaluation shall not produce `valid`.
    64	
    65	**REQ-P-CANDIDATE-005**: A repair is a new compression candidate with new
    66	content identity. Revalidation of identical compression and binding bytes under
    67	the exact same dependency shall reproduce the same report and index.
    68	
    69	**REQ-P-CANDIDATE-009**: `valid` shall require the emitted index to bind the

    71	references, logical populations, and total source routes. An index over another
    72	compression is invalid.

    80	unresolved source or frame URIs, ungrounded items, and broken residual re-entry.

    82	**REQ-P-CANDIDATE-008**: A valid working candidate may be used and dogfooded

    84	carrier admission, or Product release.

   105	## Technical triage and promotion policy
   106	
   107	The current promotion boundary is advancement of the RC2-based STDO
   108	Representation `2.5.0` source into one frozen publication-ready candidate or,
   109	under a separate publication grant, an immutable RC. Product shape, the
   110	accepted RC1 Product, and historical releases remain outside that boundary.
   111	
   112	Reviewer grades consequence under this descending severity scale:
   113	
   114	| Severity | Project meaning |
   115	|---|---|
   116	| `S0` | catastrophic, non-waivable authority, integrity, safety, or data-loss failure |
   117	| `S1` | critical mandatory-Product or method outcome, or hard-stop failure, without adequate containment |
   118	| `S2` | major semantic, authority, proportionality, dependency, or proof defect with a bounded workaround |
   119	| `S3` | minor or local ambiguity or evidence defect without mandatory-outcome loss |
   120	| `S4` | editorial, cosmetic, or otherwise non-material observation |
   121	
   122	For every finding, Reviewer returns the affected claim and observed failure,
   123	exact evidence routes, severity, causal assessment and confidence where
   124	supportable, blast radius, workaround or containment, repair complexity,
   125	regression and dependency risk, and residual uncertainty. Missing support stays
   126	explicit. An adjacent observation outside the evaluated claim is returned
   127	separately with claim-relative triage `not_applicable`; it does not replace the
   128	claim result or create a promotion block by severity alone.
   129	
   130	Executive alone assigns response priority under this descending scale:
   131	
   132	| Priority | Project meaning and current-boundary effect |
   133	|---|---|
   134	| `P0` | emergency; stop immediately and block the current promotion boundary |
   135	| `P1` | critical; block the current promotion boundary |
   136	| `P2` | high; block the current promotion boundary |
   137	| `P3` | planned; does not by itself block the current promotion boundary |
   138	| `P4` | backlog; does not block the current promotion boundary |
   139	| `P5` | observe or take no action; does not block the current promotion boundary |
   140	
   141	The project decision cutoff is `P2`: `P0` through `P2` block current
   142	promotion, while `P3` through `P5` do not automatically block it. Severity,
   143	priority, Reference Frame Method result, promotion-boundary effect, and
   144	disposition remain distinct; no numeric severity mechanically selects a
   145	priority or disposition.
   146	
   147	The cutoff cannot waive a non-waivable hard stop. Hard stops are
   148	`invalid_basis`; an unresolved authority, identity, Product-member,
   149	dependency, integrity, safety, or data-loss failure; falsification of a
   150	mandatory current-boundary claim; and `indeterminate` or `out_of_frame` on a
   151	mandatory current-boundary claim until a capable evaluation closes it.
   152	
   153	When evidence or evaluator capability cannot support technical triage,
   154	Reviewer returns `indeterminate`, names the missing evidence or capability,
   155	and preserves the residual. Executive may hold the boundary or activate or
   156	refine a capable evaluation; it may not invent, repair, or silently complete
   157	Reviewer triage. Acting under existing Product authority, Executive consumes
   158	the closed result and complete Product view, assigns priority, determines the
   159	promotion-boundary effect, and selects only an authorized disposition and next
   160	action.

   306

1	# The STDO Axiomatic Calculus for Governed Symbolic Systems
     2	
     3	## Position
     4	
     5	The **STDO Axiomatic Calculus for Governed Symbolic Systems**, written `a_c`,
     6	is STDO's domain-specific, carrier-neutral constitutional calculus for
     7	representing and relating governed symbolic systems.
     8	
     9	Its stable concept identity is:
    10	
    11	```text
    12	urn:stdo:concept:axiomatic-calculus:a-c
    13	```
    14	
    15	This standard owns that concept in bounded context:
    16	
    17	```text
    18	urn:stdo:bounded-context:axiomatic-calculus
    19	```
    20	
    21	`a_c` is a separately identifiable calculus derived from STDO principles. It
    22	defines sorts, typed objects, relations, constraints, latitude, residual
    23	uncertainty, traversals, functor kinds, judgments, closure, projections,
    24	transformations, models, and validity laws. Those definitions do not depend on
    25	a derivation-source record layout, a selected subject interpretation, a
    26	particular carrier, a model provider, a runtime, or a repository topology.

   755	  -> M_subject* | hold | gap | refusal

   761	The interpretation contract declares:

   819	
   820	The three governed layers are:

   822	```text
   823	a_c       = the pure calculus
   824	a_c.X     = subject X interpreted as a model of a_c
   825	a_c.X.C   = that accepted model encoded in carrier C

   830	```text
   831	M_X = Interpret_a_c(X)
   832	J_X = Accept_X(M_X) -> accepted | refuse
   833	G_C = Encode_C(M_X, J_X) where J_X = accepted
   834	D_C = F_D[v_carrier_admission](G_C, Profile_C, CarrierBasis_C)
   835	      -> admitted | refuse

   840	judgment subject identity and digest and `M_X`; hold or refusal cannot be
   841	encoded. `D_C` is a judgment over unchanged carrier bytes. It is not a
   842	transformed carrier. The admitted encoding evidence relation is the exact
   843	triple `(G_C, J_X, D_C)`; neither judgment enters the identity of its subject.

     1	# Reference Frame Method
     2	
     3	## Canonical Compression
     4	
     5	A human or computational actor has finite context, finite attention, finite
     6	time, and bounded capability. A material workspace may contain more relevant
     7	truth, history, topology, authority, and evidence than one actor can evaluate
     8	at once.
     9	
    10	The Reference Frame Method makes that limit explicit:
    11	
    12	```text
    13	declared evaluation family
    14	  + exact workspace and topology basis
    15	  + finite material relations and coordinates
    16	  + applicable invariants and authorities
    17	  + admissible evidence and exclusions
    18	  + actor capability envelope
    19	  = activated reference frame
    20	  -> satisfied | falsified | indeterminate | out_of_frame | invalid_basis
    21	```
    22	
    23	A project engages a body of work through a declared frame set:
    24	
    25	```text
    26	workspace and governed outcome
    27	  + accumulated practice and historical failures
    28	  + available actor capabilities
    29	  + human judgment
    30	  -> declared frame set
    31	  -> bounded evaluations
    32	  -> conjunction or translation where required
    33	  -> coverage ledger and residual uncertainty
    34	  -> empirical frame-set revision
    35	```
    36	
    37	The reference frame is the atomic engagement unit. Frame-set selection,
    38	activation, evaluation, conjunction, translation, coverage, and revision are
    39	separate method functions. A frame does not need to contain a universal theory
    40	of its possible relationships before it can support a bounded evaluation.
    41	
    42	`Atomic engagement unit` names the unit that can be activated and evaluated as
    43	one bounded context. It does not assert that every relation inside the frame is
    44	one irreducible semantic atom. A frame may carry several semantic atoms and
    45	several owner relations without merging their meaning or authority.

    56	This is an engagement meta-method. It does not define an application profile,

    77	## Core Claims
    78	
    79	1. No finite actor is presumed to hold the complete material workspace in
    80	   active attention.
    81	2. A useful frame is finite and sufficient for a declared evaluation family.
    82	3. The evaluations to be made determine the material attention surface.
    83	4. Human authority may declare a practical project frame set from accumulated
    84	   practice without deriving a unique frame partition mechanically.
    85	5. Frames may overlap, compose, refine, restrict, translate, or succeed one

   101	## Definitions
   102	
   103	### Evaluation
   104	
   105	An **evaluation** is a declared question whose admissible result family,
   106	evidence basis, decision authority, and operation authority where it performs a
   107	material action are known. An evaluation may ask for a judgment, prediction,
   108	construction, comparison, proof, refusal, classification, or action
   109	recommendation.
   110	
   111	An evaluation family groups questions that require the same material relation
   112	manifold, authority basis, and result algebra. Similar wording does not prove
   113	that two evaluations belong to the same family.
   114	
   115	### Workspace
   227	### Capability envelope
   228	
   229	A **capability envelope** declares the competence, context capacity, tools,
   230	access, applicable evaluation- or assurance-independence conditions, and
   231	configuration required to activate a frame and perform its evaluations.
   232	
   233	The same frame may be usable by one actor and unusable by another. Actor
   234	capability may justify a different frame size or activation sequence. It cannot
   235	waive an invariant or widen authority.
   236	
   237	### Reference frame
   238	
   239	A **reference frame** is a finite specification of the attention, coordinates,
   240	authority, evidence, and result relations required to perform one declared
   241	evaluation family over a stated basis.
   242	
   243	Formally, a frame may be described as:
   244	
   245	\[
   246	F = \langle Q, B, M, C, I, A, E, X, R, J, K, D \rangle
   247	\]
   248	
   249	where:
   250	
   251	- \(Q\) is the evaluation family;
   252	- \(B\) is the workspace and topology basis;
   253	- \(M\) is the material-relation manifold;
   254	- \(C\) is the coordinate and equality law;
   255	- \(I\) is the applicable invariant set;
   256	- \(A\) is the authority relation;
   257	- \(E\) is the admissible evidence and provenance law;
   258	- \(X\) is the exclusion and prohibited-assumption set;
   259	- \(R\) is the closed result algebra;
   260	- \(J\) is the invalidation and rechart condition;
   261	- \(K\) is the actor capability envelope; and
   262	- \(D\) is the optional set of declared dependencies, overlaps, inputs, and
   263	  outputs involving other frames.
   264	
   265	This tuple specifies the relation. It is not a required schema or runtime
   266	carrier.
   267	
   268	Operationally, a reference frame is an evaluation contract that defines the
   269	finite attention scope required for one evaluation family. A prompt, context
   270	packet, symbolic program, or other representation is a projection of an
   271	activated frame, not the frame itself. A frame is bound when every material
   272	coordinate above resolves to an exact source, subject, basis, authority,
   273	evidence route, actor envelope, result relation, and invalidation condition.
   274	The binding may be expressed entirely in source-linked prose; representation
   275	cannot create, widen, or replace it.
   276	
   277	### Activated frame
   278	
   279	An **activated frame** binds one frame declaration to an exact evaluation,
   280	workspace subject, basis, actor, and evidence acquisition boundary. A reusable
   281	frame declaration is not evidence that a particular activation was correct.
   282	
   283	### Frame set
   284	
   285	A **frame set** is the human-declared family of frames available for a governed
   286	outcome or workspace. It may intentionally contain overlaps, alternatives,
   287	specialist frames, broad exploratory frames, and separately activated assurance
   288	frames.
   289	
   290	A frame set is not required to be a partition, tree, stack, or exhaustive
   291	ontology.
   292	
   293	### Active frame configuration
   294	
   295	An **active frame configuration** is the set of frame activations and declared
   296	result relations used for one evaluation or decision. It may contain one frame
   297	or several disjoint, overlapping, or composed frames. Separately activated
   298	evaluations may be disjoint or overlapping.
   299	
   300	### Lens
   301	
   302	A **lens** is a reusable family of questions applied across a frame
   303	configuration. Authority, capability and reuse, temporal behavior, transport,
   304	and proof are examples of lenses when named abstractly.
   305	
   306	A lens becomes a frame only when it is instantiated with a bounded evaluation,
   307	basis, material manifold, evidence, authorities, result algebra, and capability
   308	envelope.
   309	
   310	### Role, persona, abstraction, and component
   311	
   312	A **role** allocates responsibility or authority. A **persona** alters an
   313	actor's approach or salience. An **abstraction** hides or contracts detail. A
   314	**component** is a structural part of a subject.
   315	
   316	Each may help construct or activate a frame. None is a reference frame by
   317	identity alone. One component may appear in several frames, and one frame may
   318	cross several components.

   321	
   322	## Reference Frame Laws
   323	
   324	### RF-001 Evaluation Relativity
   325	
   326	Every frame declares the evaluation family it supports. A frame with no
   327	declared evaluation family has no testable sufficiency boundary.
   328	
   329	### RF-002 Finite Attention
   330	
   331	An activated frame contains a finite attention surface that fits the selected
   332	actor's declared capability envelope. A frame that requires undeclared ambient
   333	memory, conversation history, or an effectively global workspace context is
   334	not reconstructable for that actor.
   335	
   336	### RF-003 Material Sufficiency
   337	
   338	Every known relation whose lawful change can alter the evaluation result,
   339	basis validity, evidence sufficiency, operation authority, or decision
   340	authority appears in the frame or enters through a declared authoritative
   341	input.
   342	
   343	Omitting a material relation makes the frame insufficient. The method does not
   344	require proving that no undiscovered material relation exists.
   345	
   346	### RF-004 Irrelevance Exclusion
   347	
   348	Relations that cannot affect the declared evaluation remain outside active
   349	attention unless they are required to establish irrelevance. A frame does not
   350	expand merely because adjacent workspace material exists.
   351	
   352	### RF-005 Exact Basis And Coordinates
   353	
   354	Every result binds its exact subject, basis, coordinates, and evidence scope.
   355	A stale, advanced, ambiguous, or mismatched basis returns `invalid_basis` or
   356	requires reactivation. Apparent equality does not substitute for declared
   357	coordinate equality.
   358	
   359	### RF-006 Authority Conservation
   360	
   361	A frame carries and applies admitted authority. It does not mint, widen,
   362	transfer, or reconstruct semantic, evaluation, operation, or decision authority
   363	from actor identity, available capability, evidence shape, implementation
   364	reachability, or frame selection.
   365	
   366	### RF-007 Semantic, Evidence, And Verdict Separation
   367	
   368	Semantic law defines what the evaluation means. Evidence supplies observations.
   369	The evaluator applies the declared relation. Where the evaluation performs a
   370	material operation, the existing operation owner supplies the exact grant.
   371	Decision authority disposes the result. A frame declaration keeps these roles
   372	distinguishable even when one actor lawfully performs several of them.
   373	
   374	### RF-008 Overlap Without Identity Collapse
   375	
   376	Frames may share entities, variables, evidence, or coordinates. Shared material
   377	does not establish identical meaning, basis, authority, or result. Every
   378	cross-frame equality or translation used by an evaluation is declared where it
   379	is needed.
   380	
   381	### RF-009 No Assumed Hierarchy
   382	
   383	Frames may relate through disjointness, overlap, refinement, restriction,
   384	translation, temporal succession, composition, or governance. Parent and child
   385	relations apply only where explicitly declared.
   386	
   387	Functional decomposition, authority precedence, frame configuration, subject
   388	topology, and evaluation dependency are distinct relation structures. A
   389	consumer may align them where the governed subject warrants it. It may not
   390	silently treat them as one hierarchy.
   391	
   392	### RF-010 Composition On Demand
   393	
   394	Using several frames does not require composing their internal manifolds.
   395	Composition law is required only when the governing evaluation combines their
   396	internal variables, transports evidence or values across them, or treats their
   397	operations as one material execution relation.
   398	
   399	Independently activated evaluations may instead return closed results to one
   400	declared conjunction or decision rule.
   401	
   402	### RF-011 Topology Mutation And Recharting
   403	
   404	An activated frame declares the topology changes capable of invalidating its
   405	coordinates or materiality judgment. A detected material topology mutation
   406	causes reevaluation, frame revision, or recharting before the previous result
   407	is reused.
   408	
   409	### RF-012 Closed Results
   410	
   411	Every evaluation returns a member of its declared result algebra. The baseline
   412	result family is:
   413	
   414	- `satisfied`: the declared predicate holds on the exact basis;
   415	- `falsified`: a declared counterexample defeats it;
   416	- `indeterminate`: available admissible evidence cannot decide it;
   417	- `out_of_frame`: the evaluation requires an undeclared material relation or
   418	  capability; or
   419	- `invalid_basis`: the subject or basis cannot support the evaluation.

   421	An externally owned compatible extension may refine this algebra while
   422	preserving explicit indeterminate, out-of-frame, and invalid-basis pressure.

   424	### RF-013 Reconstructable Activation
   425	
   426	A fresh competent actor inside the declared capability envelope can reconstruct
   427	the activated evaluation from the frame declaration, exact subject, basis, and
   428	admissible inputs without undocumented conversational or historical context.

   430	### RF-014 Capability Fit
   431	
   432	Frame adequacy includes actor usability. When the material manifold exceeds an
   433	actor's capability envelope, human authority may select another actor, refine
   434	the frame, sequence activations, or provide a lawful compression. The actor may
   435	not silently omit material relations to fit context.

   437	### RF-015 Residual Uncertainty
   438	
   439	Coverage and evaluation results retain known uncertainty. Unresolved relations,
   440	uncovered evaluations, contested evidence, and unknown capability remain
   441	explicit. Absence of a recorded counterexample is not evidence of universal
   442	completeness.

   444	### RF-016 Implementation Neutrality
   445	
   446	This method requires the declared relations and observable outcomes. It does
   447	not require a frame runtime, universal carrier, registry, controller, prompt
   448	format, repository layout, collaboration topology, worker count, or software

   451	### RF-017 Proportional Compression
   452	
   453	A frame compresses accumulated practice when its declaration preserves the
   454	material distinctions and failure detections required by its evaluation family

   458	retained where it supplies independently activated evaluation, different

   602	
   603	The result identifies the frame and activation, subject, basis, evaluation,

   614	- select another actor inside the frame's capability envelope;
   615	- activate another existing frame;
   616	- refine or extend a frame declaration;
   617	- revise the frame set;
   618	- change the evaluation; or

   232	## Executive Attention, Evaluation, And Action
   233	
   234	Executive is the profile frame for three inseparable duties over one governed
   235	outcome:
   236	
   237	1. **attention management** maintains the exact outcome and basis, Product-role
   238	   map, evaluation inventory, dependency relation, unresolved frontier, actor
   239	   envelopes, current MVP or release mandate, applicable triage policy, and
   240	   residual boundary, then selects the smallest
   241	   dependency-ready activation set sufficient for the next decision within the
   242	   finite actor envelopes;
   243	2. **evaluation orchestration** activates capable Workers, Reviewers, or
   244	   specialists, preserves their exact subjects and bases, and consumes only
   245	   closed results or declared translations; and
   246	3. **authorized action selection** assigns priority, determines the effect on
   247	   the current promotion boundary, applies an existing disposition, and issues
   248	   only the next already-authorized activation or action.
   249	
   250	Executive does not contain the complete workspace, perform every evaluation,
   251	or acquire Product meaning, implementation, mutation, acceptance, publication,
   252	or other operation authority from the role. A material effect remains owned by
   253	the actor carrying its exact operation grant.
   254	
   255	The attention cycle is:
   256	
   257	```text
   258	U0 = every known material evaluation not closed on the current basis
   259	
   260	while U is non-empty:
   261	  select a finite dependency-ready subset M that fits the assigned actors
   262	  activate each member of M against the exact outcome and basis
   263	  keep assurance-independent evaluations free of unclosed peer results
   264	  record every closed result, technical triage, residual, and invalidation condition
   265	  apply only declared conjunctions or translations
   266	  assign priority and boundary effect only under the current Product mandate
   267	  invalidate affected results when the subject or basis changes
   268	  update U from coverage, dependencies, conflicts, and discovered materiality
   269	
   270	stop only when every mandatory evaluation is closed, or governing authority
   271	has explicitly retained every remaining residual consistently with the claim
   272	```
   273	
   274	This relation requires no scheduler or frame engine. `M` may contain parallel
   275	activations. Recursion follows declared evaluation dependencies and bounded
   276	refinements; it does not nest or join undifferentiated copies of every frame.
   277	The Executive retains the frontier and closed-result ledger in attention, not
   278	the undocumented working context of every evaluator.
   279	
   280	Severity supplied by Reviewer is evaluation evidence. Priority, current-boundary
   281	effect, `STDO-UP-020` disposition, and subsequent action are Executive decisions.
   282	They remain distinct ledger entries even when a Product-defined policy maps one
   283	to another.
   284	
   285	Every result returns to Executive, a declared conjunction, or another frame
   286	through an explicit `D` relation. No lateral handoff, child completion, model
   287	response, tool output, or shared actor implicitly activates another frame or
   288	authorizes continuation. A consumer receives the closed result and its source
   289	routes, not the child's hidden reasoning context.

   357	### Technical triage, severity, priority, and boundary effect
   358	
   359	**Technical triage** is the Reviewer-owned assessment of one finding against
   360	the exact evaluated claim and basis. Where supported by admissible evidence and
   361	the actor capability envelope, it records:
   362	
   363	- the affected claim and observed failure;
   364	- severity under the Product-selected severity scale;
   365	- causal assessment and confidence;
   366	- blast radius and affected users, paths, or relations;
   367	- available workaround or containment;
   368	- repair complexity, regression risk, and material dependencies; and
   369	- residual uncertainty and the evidence required to reduce it.
   370	
   371	Missing causal or repair evidence remains explicit. Reviewer returns
   372	`indeterminate` or `out_of_frame` pressure where the missing relation can change
   373	the evaluation; it does not invent precision or send work laterally to Worker.
   374	
   375	**Severity** grades consequence if the finding manifests. **Priority** orders
   376	response relative to the complete Product outcome, likelihood and exposure,
   377	current MVP or release mandate, reversibility, dependencies, cost of delay, and
   378	available capacity. Reviewer grades severity. Executive assigns priority.

   381	priority scale, current-boundary decision cutoff, and non-waivable hard stops.

   384	makes a finding release-blocking.

   563	`STDO-UP-020` remains the owner of assessment and semantic disposition. This
   564	profile uses the Reviewer result as independent live-surface evaluation input

   982	## Complete Engagement Transition
   983	
   984	### 1. Existing Authority Selects The Basis
   985	
   986	Goals, Product, requirements, accepted design, ticket, release, or an admitted
   987	bounded proxy selects the outcome and work authority under its existing STDO
   988	owner. The Product-owned Project Reference-Frame Basis projects that decision.
   989	
   990	### 2. Executive Activates Worker
   991	
   992	The Executive applies `REFERENCE_FRAME_METHOD.md` activation to the
   993	`STDO-UP-020` sufficient execution intake. The activation identifies:
   994	
   995	- selected complete STDO and project authority;
   996	- exact governed outcome and checkpoint;
   997	- affected causal relation set and governing invariants;
   998	- selected computational relations and specialist frames;
   999	- testing claims, exact subjects, frame topology, material combination
  1000	  populations, ordinary paths, oracles, and forbidden-path exclusions where
  1001	  testing evidence is required;
  1002	- Worker authority, capability envelope, and the exact inherited operation
  1003	  grant, subject, and write territory where mutation is authorized;
  1004	- evidence and qualification obligations;
  1005	- exclusions, prohibited competing paths, stop conditions, and re-entry
  1006	  conditions; and
  1007	- the exact bounded action already authorized.
  1008	
  1009	If activation detects a known capability, authority, subject, basis, or
  1010	topology mismatch, it returns `activation_refusal` directly to Executive. No
  1011	Worker frame is active, no Worker evaluation occurs, and Executive must not
  1012	manufacture a Worker result to represent the failed activation.
  1013	
  1014	### 3. Worker Returns To Executive
  1015	
  1016	Every Worker activation terminates in one closed work result sent to the
  1017	Executive:
  1018	
  1019	```text
  1020	WorkerResult
  1021	  = candidate_ready(exact_subject, transition_evidence, residuals)
  1022	  | refused(reason, authority, evidence)
  1023	  | incomplete(residuals, evidence, stop_basis)
  1024	  | re_entry_requested(owner, material_relation, evidence)
  1025	```
  1026	
  1027	The notation is explanatory and mandates no schema.
  1028	
  1029	Each variant accompanies exactly one Reference Frame Method result under the
  1030	mapping in `Work result`: `satisfied -> candidate_ready`, `falsified ->
  1031	refused`, `indeterminate -> incomplete`, and `out_of_frame | invalid_basis ->
  1032	re_entry_requested`. The mapping applies only after lawful activation.
  1033	
  1034	The Worker does not send a candidate directly into an implicitly active
  1035	Reviewer. It stops after returning the result.
  1036	
  1037	### 4. Executive Evaluates The Work Result
  1038	
  1039	For `refused`, `incomplete`, or `re_entry_requested`, the Executive verifies
  1040	the exact basis and applies the existing authority relation. It records the
  1041	applicable `STDO-UP-020` disposition or reactivates work only when the current
  1042	authority already permits that action. None of these variants can be treated as
  1043	accepted progress merely because work occurred.
  1044	
  1045	For `candidate_ready`, the Executive verifies the exact subject and determines
  1046	whether independent assessment is required by `STDO-UP-007`,
  1047	`STDO-UP-020`, `STDO-UP-022`, Product, release, risk, or the admitted work
  1048	contract. Green aggregate status cannot satisfy this step when a required
  1049	user-acceptance, end-to-end, integration, unit, or negative-path result is
  1050	missing, bound to another subject, or contradicted by a material frame result.
  1051	
  1052	### 5A. Candidate Does Not Require Independent Review
  1053	
  1054	When independent review is not required, the Executive consumes the exact
  1055	candidate, Worker self-review, transition evidence, and any mandatory
  1056	specialist-frame results. It applies `STDO-UP-020` disposition within its
  1057	decision envelope.
  1058	
  1059	Self-review remains Worker evidence. The disposition does not relabel it as
  1060	independent.
  1061	
  1062	### 5B. Candidate Requires Independent Review
  1063	
  1064	When independent review is required, the Executive activates the Reviewer with:
  1065	
  1066	- exact candidate and governing basis;
  1067	- exact claim, composition boundary, population, scope, and exclusions;
  1068	- applicable STDO and project authority;
  1069	- required evidence and ordinary assurance path;
  1070	- required user-acceptance, end-to-end, integration, unit, combinatorial, and
  1071	  negative-path frame results with their exact claims and populations;
  1072	- the Product-selected severity scale and exact affected Product claims;
  1073	- Reviewer capability and independence envelope; and
  1074	- invalidation and stop conditions.
  1075	
  1076	The candidate is frozen before material reference exposure where
  1077	`STDO-UP-022` requires it. Otherwise the subject is stabilized to the exactness
  1078	required by `STDO-UP-007`, `STDO-UP-020`, and the claim.
  1079	
  1080	### 6. Reviewer Returns To Executive
  1081	
  1082	The Reviewer returns one closed evaluation containing:
  1083	
  1084	- frame and activation identity;
  1085	- exact subject, basis, claim, scope, exclusions, and evaluated population;
  1086	- Reviewer actor and independence conditions;
  1087	- evidence and ordinary assurance path acquired;
  1088	- Reference Frame Method result;
  1089	- findings, counterexamples, and adjacent observations;
  1090	- for each finding, affected claim, severity, causal assessment and confidence,
  1091	  blast radius, workaround, repair complexity, regression risk, and residual
  1092	  uncertainty where supportable; and
  1093	- invalidation conditions and re-entry owner where applicable.
  1094	
  1095	### Reviewer Result And Triage Projection
  1096	
  1097	The Reviewer payload projection is total across the Reference Frame Method
  1098	result algebra. `complete`, `indeterminate`, and `not_applicable` below classify
  1099	the finding-level triage payload; they are not new evaluation results,
  1100	dispositions, priorities, or lifecycle states.
  1101	
  1102	| Reference Frame Method result | Finding and triage payload | Executive consumption constraint |
  1103	|---|---|---|
  1104	| `satisfied` | explicit no-finding state; triage `not_applicable`; evidence, residuals, and invalidation remain present | priority and current-boundary effect are `not_applicable` to this review result unless another exact consumed result supplies a finding |
  1105	| `falsified` | one or more exact findings; triage is `complete` where supported and preserves `indeterminate` fields where evidence cannot close them | apply Product-owned priority and boundary policy without mechanically mapping severity to disposition |
  1106	| `indeterminate` | partial finding or observation state; triage `indeterminate`; exact evidence gaps and residual uncertainty | retain uncertainty or reactivate a capable evaluation; do not consume it as satisfaction or a closed finding |
  1107	| `out_of_frame` | the evaluated claim requires an undeclared material relation or evaluator capability; triage `indeterminate`; name the missing relation or capability and exact reconfiguration pressure | refine or reconfigure a capable activation and retain the claim as unresolved; do not consume the result as satisfaction or falsification |
  1108	| `invalid_basis` | basis failure; triage `not_applicable`; invalidation evidence and basis-repair pressure | refuse result consumption and return through the declared basis re-entry relation |
  1109	
  1110	An adjacent observation outside the evaluated claim does not replace the
  1111	claim-relative result. Reviewer returns it separately with triage
  1112	`not_applicable` to that claim and exact repricing or re-entry pressure. The
  1113	Executive returns it to its declared owner without creating a claim-relative
  1114	block or another review round from severity alone.
  1115	
  1116	The Reviewer returns to Executive, not Worker. It does not edit the candidate,
  1117	direct the repair, or authorize continuation.
  1118	
  1119	### 7. Executive Disposes And Checkpoints
  1120	
  1121	The Executive verifies that every consumed result remains bound to the current
  1122	subject and basis, revalidates the complete Product view and current MVP or
  1123	release mandate, applies any declared result conjunction, assigns priority,
  1124	records the effect on the current promotion boundary, and acts on exactly one
  1125	`STDO-UP-020` disposition within its grant:
  1126	
  1127	- `accept`;
  1128	- `local_repair`;
  1129	- `re_enter`; or
  1130	- `reject`.
  1131	
  1132	`STDO-UP-020` remains the owner of each disposition, exact accepted checkpoint,
  1133	and next already-authorized bounded action. A repair creates a new candidate.
  1134	An affected review is reactivated against that candidate. Acceptance does not
  1135	widen the Product outcome or authorize an unselected successor.
  1136	
  1137	Severity does not mechanically select priority or block promotion. Priority
  1138	does not erase severity or waive a hard stop. The Executive determines blocking
  1139	from the exact affected claim, current mandate, applicable hard stops, and
  1140	Product-owned cutoff policy. An unsupported technical assessment is returned
  1141	through a new or refined activation rather than silently rewritten.
  1142	
  1143	### Executive Promotion Constraint Projection
  1144	
  1145	| Consumed condition | Required Executive constraint |
  1146	|---|---|
  1147	| valid falsification of a mandatory claim governed by a non-waivable hard stop | current promotion boundary blocks regardless of assigned priority or decision cutoff |
  1148	| valid finding below the Product-owned decision cutoff with no hard stop | no mechanical block follows; apply the Product-owned policy and retain any accepted residual explicitly |
  1149	| observation outside the exact evaluated claim | treat as bounded repricing or re-entry input; do not create a claim-relative block or another review round by severity label |
  1150	| unsupported or materially incomplete technical assessment | reactivate a capable evaluation or retain `indeterminate`; do not rewrite Reviewer evidence |

  1340	protocol.
  1341	
  1342	The profile trial evaluates both this profile and its declared composition with
  1343	the exact Reference Frame Method basis without reproducing either as peer
  1344	authority. A valid pure-method trial does not prove this profile, and a valid
  1345	profile trial does not prove the method's complete function population.
  1346	
  1347	Mechanical document checks may protect exact table shape, result cardinality,
  1348	source-digest congruence, and named refusal boundaries. They do not establish

49	## Position
    50	
    51	This method governs how finite actors construct and use bounded reasoning or
    52	execution contexts over a changing body of work. It applies to human work,
    53	agentic work, deterministic evaluation, probabilistic construction, assurance,
    54	and mixed work where the governing product or method permits them.
    55	
    56	This is an engagement meta-method. It does not define an application profile,
    57	role mapping, Product-owned frame-basis binding, domain Product, specification
    58	taxonomy, design ontology, runtime, workflow, adoption relation, or assurance
    59	implementation. External methods and Products may import or specialize these
    60	relations under their own authority. That external relation does not enter or
    61	amend the principles.
    62	
    63	`REFERENCE_FRAME_METHOD.md` owns the reference-frame-evaluation bounded context
    64	`urn:stdo:bounded-context:reference-frame-evaluation` under its exact
    65	publication basis. This standard owns only its frame declaration, activation,
    66	evaluation, basis, relation, result, coverage, revision, and qualification
    67	concepts. A same-spelled profile, Product, role, or runtime carrier is not
    68	imported by proximity or nominal match.
    69	
    70	The method is substrate-neutral. A reference frame may be represented in prose,
    71	structured data, a prompt, a design asset, a typed carrier, a runtime context,
    72	or another form selected by its consumer. No class, aggregate, actor,
    73	controller, service, registry, graph, or frame engine is required.

    77	## Core Claims
    78	
    79	1. No finite actor is presumed to hold the complete material workspace in
    80	   active attention.
    81	2. A useful frame is finite and sufficient for a declared evaluation family.
    82	3. The evaluations to be made determine the material attention surface.
    83	4. Human authority may declare a practical project frame set from accumulated
    84	   practice without deriving a unique frame partition mechanically.
    85	5. Frames may overlap, compose, refine, restrict, translate, or succeed one
    86	   another. Hierarchy is one optional relation.
    87	6. Several frames may be used together without composing their internal
    88	   coordinate systems.
    89	7. Coverage is relative to a declared workspace, governed outcome, evaluation
    90	   inventory, basis, and time.

    92	   decision authority from its breadth, usefulness, actor, or implementation
    93	   technology.
    94	9. Unknown and out-of-frame results are lawful pressure for reconfiguration.
    95	   They are not failed evaluations or implied acceptance.

   102	
   103	### Evaluation
   104	
   105	An **evaluation** is a declared question whose admissible result family,
   106	evidence basis, decision authority, and operation authority where it performs a
   107	material action are known. An evaluation may ask for a judgment, prediction,
   108	construction, comparison, proof, refusal, classification, or action
   109	recommendation.
   110	
   111	An evaluation family groups questions that require the same material relation
   112	manifold, authority basis, and result algebra. Similar wording does not prove
   113	that two evaluations belong to the same family.
   114	
   115	### Workspace
   227	### Capability envelope
   228	
   229	A **capability envelope** declares the competence, context capacity, tools,
   230	access, applicable evaluation- or assurance-independence conditions, and
   231	configuration required to activate a frame and perform its evaluations.
   232	
   233	The same frame may be usable by one actor and unusable by another. Actor
   234	capability may justify a different frame size or activation sequence. It cannot
   235	waive an invariant or widen authority.
   236	
   237	### Reference frame
   238	
   239	A **reference frame** is a finite specification of the attention, coordinates,
   240	authority, evidence, and result relations required to perform one declared
   241	evaluation family over a stated basis.
   242	
   243	Formally, a frame may be described as:
   244	
   245	\[
   246	F = \langle Q, B, M, C, I, A, E, X, R, J, K, D \rangle
   247	\]
   248	
   249	where:
   250	
   251	- \(Q\) is the evaluation family;
   252	- \(B\) is the workspace and topology basis;
   253	- \(M\) is the material-relation manifold;
   254	- \(C\) is the coordinate and equality law;
   255	- \(I\) is the applicable invariant set;
   256	- \(A\) is the authority relation;
   257	- \(E\) is the admissible evidence and provenance law;
   258	- \(X\) is the exclusion and prohibited-assumption set;
   259	- \(R\) is the closed result algebra;
   260	- \(J\) is the invalidation and rechart condition;
   261	- \(K\) is the actor capability envelope; and
   262	- \(D\) is the optional set of declared dependencies, overlaps, inputs, and
   263	  outputs involving other frames.
   264	
   265	This tuple specifies the relation. It is not a required schema or runtime
   266	carrier.
   267	
   268	Operationally, a reference frame is an evaluation contract that defines the
   269	finite attention scope required for one evaluation family. A prompt, context
   270	packet, symbolic program, or other representation is a projection of an
   271	activated frame, not the frame itself. A frame is bound when every material
   272	coordinate above resolves to an exact source, subject, basis, authority,
   273	evidence route, actor envelope, result relation, and invalidation condition.
   274	The binding may be expressed entirely in source-linked prose; representation
   275	cannot create, widen, or replace it.
   276	
   277	### Activated frame
   278	
   279	An **activated frame** binds one frame declaration to an exact evaluation,
   280	workspace subject, basis, actor, and evidence acquisition boundary. A reusable
   281	frame declaration is not evidence that a particular activation was correct.
   282	
   283	### Frame set
   284	
   285	A **frame set** is the human-declared family of frames available for a governed
   286	outcome or workspace. It may intentionally contain overlaps, alternatives,
   287	specialist frames, broad exploratory frames, and separately activated assurance
   288	frames.
   289	
   290	A frame set is not required to be a partition, tree, stack, or exhaustive
   291	ontology.
   292	
   293	### Active frame configuration
   294	
   295	An **active frame configuration** is the set of frame activations and declared
   296	result relations used for one evaluation or decision. It may contain one frame
   297	or several disjoint, overlapping, or composed frames. Separately activated
   298	evaluations may be disjoint or overlapping.
   299	
   300	### Lens
   301	
   302	A **lens** is a reusable family of questions applied across a frame
   303	configuration. Authority, capability and reuse, temporal behavior, transport,
   304	and proof are examples of lenses when named abstractly.
   305	
   306	A lens becomes a frame only when it is instantiated with a bounded evaluation,
   307	basis, material manifold, evidence, authorities, result algebra, and capability
   308	envelope.
   309	
   310	### Role, persona, abstraction, and component
   311	
   312	A **role** allocates responsibility or authority. A **persona** alters an
   313	actor's approach or salience. An **abstraction** hides or contracts detail. A
   314	**component** is a structural part of a subject.
   315	
   316	Each may help construct or activate a frame. None is a reference frame by
   317	identity alone. One component may appear in several frames, and one frame may
   318	cross several components.
   319

   321	
   322	## Reference Frame Laws
   323	
   324	### RF-001 Evaluation Relativity
   325	
   326	Every frame declares the evaluation family it supports. A frame with no
   327	declared evaluation family has no testable sufficiency boundary.
   328	
   329	### RF-002 Finite Attention
   330	
   331	An activated frame contains a finite attention surface that fits the selected
   332	actor's declared capability envelope. A frame that requires undeclared ambient
   333	memory, conversation history, or an effectively global workspace context is
   334	not reconstructable for that actor.
   335	
   336	### RF-003 Material Sufficiency
   337	
   338	Every known relation whose lawful change can alter the evaluation result,
   339	basis validity, evidence sufficiency, operation authority, or decision
   340	authority appears in the frame or enters through a declared authoritative
   341	input.
   342	
   343	Omitting a material relation makes the frame insufficient. The method does not
   344	require proving that no undiscovered material relation exists.
   345	
   346	### RF-004 Irrelevance Exclusion
   347	
   348	Relations that cannot affect the declared evaluation remain outside active
   349	attention unless they are required to establish irrelevance. A frame does not
   350	expand merely because adjacent workspace material exists.
   351	
   352	### RF-005 Exact Basis And Coordinates
   353	
   354	Every result binds its exact subject, basis, coordinates, and evidence scope.
   355	A stale, advanced, ambiguous, or mismatched basis returns `invalid_basis` or
   356	requires reactivation. Apparent equality does not substitute for declared
   357	coordinate equality.
   358	
   359	### RF-006 Authority Conservation
   360	
   361	A frame carries and applies admitted authority. It does not mint, widen,
   362	transfer, or reconstruct semantic, evaluation, operation, or decision authority
   363	from actor identity, available capability, evidence shape, implementation
   364	reachability, or frame selection.
   365	
   366	### RF-007 Semantic, Evidence, And Verdict Separation
   367	
   368	Semantic law defines what the evaluation means. Evidence supplies observations.
   369	The evaluator applies the declared relation. Where the evaluation performs a
   370	material operation, the existing operation owner supplies the exact grant.
   371	Decision authority disposes the result. A frame declaration keeps these roles
   372	distinguishable even when one actor lawfully performs several of them.
   373	
   374	### RF-008 Overlap Without Identity Collapse
   375	
   376	Frames may share entities, variables, evidence, or coordinates. Shared material
   377	does not establish identical meaning, basis, authority, or result. Every
   378	cross-frame equality or translation used by an evaluation is declared where it
   379	is needed.
   380	
   381	### RF-009 No Assumed Hierarchy
   382	
   383	Frames may relate through disjointness, overlap, refinement, restriction,
   384	translation, temporal succession, composition, or governance. Parent and child
   385	relations apply only where explicitly declared.
   386	
   387	Functional decomposition, authority precedence, frame configuration, subject
   388	topology, and evaluation dependency are distinct relation structures. A
   389	consumer may align them where the governed subject warrants it. It may not
   390	silently treat them as one hierarchy.
   391	
   392	### RF-010 Composition On Demand
   393	
   394	Using several frames does not require composing their internal manifolds.
   395	Composition law is required only when the governing evaluation combines their
   396	internal variables, transports evidence or values across them, or treats their
   397	operations as one material execution relation.
   398	
   399	Independently activated evaluations may instead return closed results to one
   400	declared conjunction or decision rule.
   401	
   402	### RF-011 Topology Mutation And Recharting
   403	
   404	An activated frame declares the topology changes capable of invalidating its
   405	coordinates or materiality judgment. A detected material topology mutation
   406	causes reevaluation, frame revision, or recharting before the previous result
   407	is reused.
   408	
   409	### RF-012 Closed Results
   410	
   411	Every evaluation returns a member of its declared result algebra. The baseline
   412	result family is:
   413	
   414	- `satisfied`: the declared predicate holds on the exact basis;
   415	- `falsified`: a declared counterexample defeats it;
   416	- `indeterminate`: available admissible evidence cannot decide it;
   417	- `out_of_frame`: the evaluation requires an undeclared material relation or
   418	  capability; or
   419	- `invalid_basis`: the subject or basis cannot support the evaluation.
   420	
   421	An externally owned compatible extension may refine this algebra while
   422	preserving explicit indeterminate, out-of-frame, and invalid-basis pressure.
   423	
   424	### RF-013 Reconstructable Activation
   425	
   426	A fresh competent actor inside the declared capability envelope can reconstruct
   427	the activated evaluation from the frame declaration, exact subject, basis, and
   428	admissible inputs without undocumented conversational or historical context.
   429	
   430	### RF-014 Capability Fit
   431	
   432	Frame adequacy includes actor usability. When the material manifold exceeds an
   433	actor's capability envelope, human authority may select another actor, refine
   434	the frame, sequence activations, or provide a lawful compression. The actor may
   435	not silently omit material relations to fit context.
   436	
   437	### RF-015 Residual Uncertainty
   438	
   439	Coverage and evaluation results retain known uncertainty. Unresolved relations,
   440	uncovered evaluations, contested evidence, and unknown capability remain
   441	explicit. Absence of a recorded counterexample is not evidence of universal
   442	completeness.
   443	
   444	### RF-016 Implementation Neutrality
   445	
   446	This method requires the declared relations and observable outcomes. It does
   447	not require a frame runtime, universal carrier, registry, controller, prompt
   448	format, repository layout, collaboration topology, worker count, or software
   449	framework.
   450	
   451	### RF-017 Proportional Compression
   452	
   453	A frame compresses accumulated practice when its declaration preserves the
   454	material distinctions and failure detections required by its evaluation family
   455	while fitting its capability envelope.
   456	
   457	Compression does not require a unique smallest frame. Intentional overlap is
   458	retained where it supplies independently activated evaluation, different
   459	capability fit, different evidence altitude, or useful fault detection. Frames
   460	are merged only when the merged frame preserves evaluation meaning, authority,
   461	capability fit, and proportional reasoning cost.
   462	
   463	### Engagement Atom And Semantic Prime
   569	## Engagement
   570	
   571	### Establish The Evaluation Basis
   572	
   573	An engagement names:
   574	
   575	- the governed outcome or decision;
   576	- the exact workspace subject and basis;
   577	- the evaluation or evaluation family;
   578	- the applicable frame-set, semantic, evaluation, operation where material,
   579	  and decision authority;
   580	- the available actor capability envelopes; and
   581	- the conditions that make the result stale or out of scope.
   582	
   583	### Select And Activate
   584	
   585	The actor or assigning authority selects one frame or one declared active frame
   586	configuration capable of the evaluation. Activation binds each reusable frame
   587	declaration to the exact subject and basis. It loads the declared material
   588	relations and evidence sources rather than an undifferentiated workspace dump.
   589	
   590	When no available frame and actor pairing can lawfully perform the evaluation,
   591	activation returns a refusal or `out_of_frame` pressure. Work does not proceed
   592	through implied context.
   593	
   594	### Evaluate
   595	
   596	The evaluator applies the frame's declared invariants, evidence rules, and
   597	result algebra. It distinguishes semantic law, observed evidence, inference,
   598	and decision. It records every assumption whose failure could change the
   599	result.
   600	
   601	### Return A Closed Result
   602	
   603	The result identifies the frame and activation, subject, basis, evaluation,
   604	actor, evidence, verdict, residual uncertainty, and invalidation conditions.
   605	The frame's internal working context does not need to be transferred when its
   606	closed result and provenance are sufficient for the consuming decision.
   607	
   608	### Reconfigure When Necessary
   609	
   610	An `out_of_frame`, invalid-basis, repeated indeterminate, or incompatible result
   611	causes one of:
   612	
   613	- supply missing admissible evidence;
   614	- select another actor inside the frame's capability envelope;
   615	- activate another existing frame;
   616	- refine or extend a frame declaration;
   617	- revise the frame set;
   618	- change the evaluation; or
   619	- re-enter the governing Product or method relation.
   620	
   621	The disposition follows the cause. A difficult evaluation alone does not prove
   622	that another frame is required.

   218	
   219	**Executive** is the profile label for the frame that selects or confirms the

   231	
   232	## Executive Attention, Evaluation, And Action
   233	
   234	Executive is the profile frame for three inseparable duties over one governed
   235	outcome:
   236	
   237	1. **attention management** maintains the exact outcome and basis, Product-role
   238	   map, evaluation inventory, dependency relation, unresolved frontier, actor
   239	   envelopes, current MVP or release mandate, applicable triage policy, and
   240	   residual boundary, then selects the smallest
   241	   dependency-ready activation set sufficient for the next decision within the
   242	   finite actor envelopes;
   243	2. **evaluation orchestration** activates capable Workers, Reviewers, or
   244	   specialists, preserves their exact subjects and bases, and consumes only
   245	   closed results or declared translations; and
   246	3. **authorized action selection** assigns priority, determines the effect on
   247	   the current promotion boundary, applies an existing disposition, and issues
   248	   only the next already-authorized activation or action.
   249	
   250	Executive does not contain the complete workspace, perform every evaluation,
   251	or acquire Product meaning, implementation, mutation, acceptance, publication,
   252	or other operation authority from the role. A material effect remains owned by
   253	the actor carrying its exact operation grant.
   254	
   255	The attention cycle is:
   256	
   257	```text
   258	U0 = every known material evaluation not closed on the current basis
   259	
   260	while U is non-empty:
   261	  select a finite dependency-ready subset M that fits the assigned actors
   262	  activate each member of M against the exact outcome and basis
   263	  keep assurance-independent evaluations free of unclosed peer results
   264	  record every closed result, technical triage, residual, and invalidation condition
   265	  apply only declared conjunctions or translations
   266	  assign priority and boundary effect only under the current Product mandate
   267	  invalidate affected results when the subject or basis changes
   268	  update U from coverage, dependencies, conflicts, and discovered materiality
   269	
   270	stop only when every mandatory evaluation is closed, or governing authority
   271	has explicitly retained every remaining residual consistently with the claim
   272	```
   273	
   274	This relation requires no scheduler or frame engine. `M` may contain parallel
   275	activations. Recursion follows declared evaluation dependencies and bounded
   276	refinements; it does not nest or join undifferentiated copies of every frame.
   277	The Executive retains the frontier and closed-result ledger in attention, not
   278	the undocumented working context of every evaluator.
   279	
   280	Severity supplied by Reviewer is evaluation evidence. Priority, current-boundary
   281	effect, `STDO-UP-020` disposition, and subsequent action are Executive decisions.
   282	They remain distinct ledger entries even when a Product-defined policy maps one
   283	to another.
   284	
   285	Every result returns to Executive, a declared conjunction, or another frame
   286	through an explicit `D` relation. No lateral handoff, child completion, model
   287	response, tool output, or shared actor implicitly activates another frame or
   288	authorizes continuation. A consumer receives the closed result and its source
   289	routes, not the child's hidden reasoning context.

   291	### Executive Drift Locks
   292	
   293	Before activation and before disposition, Executive revalidates:
   294	
   295	- **outcome lock** — selected Goal, Product outcome, boundary, and lawful
   296	  re-entry class, current MVP or release mandate, and triage policy remain
   297	  unchanged;
   298	- **basis lock** — subject, authority, dependency, configuration, topology,
   299	  evidence, time, and candidate coordinates remain exact and current;
   300	- **Product-role lock** — mutable Source Project, Product Definition,
   301	  Release Cut, Product, Install, Artifact, and dependent Product identities
   302	  remain distinct, and every Development Product role remains bound to its
   303	  exact underlying Install;
   304	- **authority lock** — semantic, evaluation, operation, decision, acceptance,

   306	- **coverage-and-return lock** — every material evaluation and interaction is

   309	
   310	Changed Product meaning requires re-entry. A stale or substituted basis is
   311	`invalid_basis`. Missing material scope is `out_of_frame`. Missing operation

   316	### Product-Chain Basis
   317	
   318	A governed outcome may concern one Product or an explicit directed chain of
   319	Products. Its basis records the distinct role of every mutable Source Project,
   320	current Product Definition, exact candidate checkpoint, Release Cut, Product,
   321	Install, Artifact, Development Product, dependent Product, and composition
   322	edge. Each Development Product role binds one exact underlying Install
   323	identity. Each edge names its source and target roles, governing authority and

   326	An installed Product may lawfully build its own successor or another Product.

   340	### Worker
   341	
   342	**Worker** is the profile label for `STDO-UP-020`'s bounded constructor role

   344	inside its exact intake through the operation authority inherited from the

   347	
   348	### Reviewer
   349	
   350	**Reviewer** is the profile label for the independent live-surface evaluation
   351	consumed by the `STDO-UP-020` assessment relation and governed by
   352	`STDO-UP-007` and `STDO-UP-022` when activated as a reference frame. It
   353	evaluates one exact subject and returns a closed result with evidence-bound
